title: fix(process): avoid Linux Gateway stalls when spawning commands
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Linux Gateway pauses when exec tools and Git helpers launch commands from a large Gateway process.

## User Impact

When the broker starts successfully, covered command launches fork a small helper instead of blocking the Gateway while Linux copies its page tables. Commands keep their existing approvals, arguments, output, and cancellation owners. The broker starts automatically for the default Node runtime on Linux; there is no new configuration or state migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

A Gateway with 5.4 GB RSS spent 15.6% of its main thread inside 56 clone calls over 20 seconds, averaging 55.6 ms each. A CPU profile attributed 34% of main-thread work to native process spawning. The remaining commands are useful work; the expensive parent is the problem.

One process-scoped spawn broker starts before the heavy Gateway runtime. Native child, service-relay, and owned-worker launches transfer real stdio sockets and forward IPC messages. Execa runs in the broker while existing collectors, admission checks, process supervisors, and tree-termination policies stay with their owners. After first readiness, broker loss fails affected requests, cleans known children, and restarts with bounded backoff; it never silently retries through local spawning. Extracted PR-tool runtimes include the required broker client dependencies. Expected steady-state Gateway main-thread clone count for covered exec/Git launches with the broker ready: **0**.

If the broker fails on its initial start (spawn/entry error, exit before readiness, or the existing 15-second readiness deadline), the Gateway logs one error with the reason and runtime entry path and uses in-process spawning for the rest of the process lifetime. It does not retry that initial failure. Once the broker has become ready, in-flight failures retain `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE` and the existing bounded recovery behavior.

Buffered execa capture uses a bounded tee to a separate output socket so execa retains its buffering and maxBuffer enforcement; that path is not zero-copy. Native and unbuffered output use transferred sockets, with bounded preservation of any pre-transfer bytes. A small adapter checks Node's private pipe read-stop contract because ordinary Socket.pause() does not stop the sender's libuv reader during IPC handoff. Command context, pending cancellation, and late PID cleanup survive the asynchronous boundary.

The broker starts in its own process group. On broker loss, the Gateway terminates that group even if an individual child's PID has not yet been reported; service relays independently retain IPC parent-loss and anchor cleanup. A detached child can survive a broker crash before its PID is reported, matching the existing Gateway-crash residual for directly spawned children. The coordinator rejected a cgroup prerequisite for this lane: the current direct-spawn design also lacks pre-spawn custody on Gateway death, while group cleanup and relay ownership cover the non-detached and tree-owned paths here. The detached fault-injection probe is retained as evidence of the documented residual.

Explicit local paths remain for numeric/anonymous descriptors, independently launched applications, CLI-only helpers, Bun, macOS, and Windows. PTY sessions, app-server lifecycles, Windows anchors, worker-thread ownership, command frequency, and approvals/redaction are outside this change.

## Evidence

- Parenting regression failed before cutover: the exec-tool adapter and runExec reported parent 30783 instead of broker 32047 (2 failed / 1 passed).
- Real-process coverage exercises large stdout/stderr and stdin, exit/signal/timeout/maxBuffer/cancel parity, inherited stdin, relay control/lineage pipes, owned-worker IPC, tree cleanup, broker crash/restart, failed launches, and parent loss.
- Additional regressions cover coalesced readiness events, early output and EOF, queued stdin closure, collection of completed proxies, callback context, and cancellation during stalled startup.
- Linux Testbox, Node 24.19.0: 34 tests passed on a pre-review candidate. A separate successful probe parented all ten commands to broker 6701 rather than host 6681; broker RSS was 97,284 KiB in source/tsx execution. The lease was stopped. This is not a post-deployment Team profile.
- The transport baseline broad runtime run passed **1,942 tests**, with 74 skipped and two native Bash fixture startup timeouts before imports completed. The unchanged three spill cases then passed once in isolation with the original timeouts; the import-only diagnostic took 13.5 seconds. No assertions or timing limits were changed. The full process suite, exec/session tools, and Gateway boot are covered; the real service lifecycle suite runs both transports.
- Process-group custody regression: unpublished non-detached native/execa children survived before the fix (2 failures), and both are gone after broker loss with the fix. All 61 broker tests passed after the final fixes; the broad run also includes them. A separate host-exit probe confirmed cleanup of a detached child that ignored TERM.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` and `git diff --check` pass after the final fixes. Regressions also cover startup IPC FIFO and recovery across seven independently healthy broker generations while preserving the consecutive-startup-failure bound. Final Codex review is **clean through P2**.

- Focused build/extracted-tooling checks passed 50 tests. Native provisioning passed 16 cases; the unchanged macOS six-worktree case exceeded its 120-second limit (207 seconds), without a module or assertion failure. This local timing gap is retained; no timeout or assertion changes were made. Changed-file checks also pass for the integration correction.


- Startup availability: 17 targeted host/context/startup/restart/Gateway tests passed, including immediate broker exit and the real 15-second deadline. Both prove one startup attempt, one error log, and native child parent PIDs across two Gateway starts. The updated full build exited zero.

- The follow-up relay ownership extraction addresses [the line-cap failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35187248481/job/105092224560) without baseline or budget changes. The relay host measures 678 counted lines on the branch and 690 when merged with main at `9edc73fc2f9` (previous merged count 707; cap 700). The host retains runtime-entry selection, generation authority, cancellation, lineage observation, and the extinction join; broker launch normalization and socket/IPC readiness now live with the broker.

- Exact-head CI for `fcff141146f88b02b6c6fb74f349f6804dfb562d` [completed successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35189483103): 142 successful jobs and 15 skips. The [baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35189483103/job/105098882159) passed. The single exact-head watch returned GREEN; no jobs were rerun.

Docs updated: `docs/gateway/background-process.md`. The only baseline change is the authorized assertion-count shrink for `src/process/exec-spawn.ts`, 4 → 3.


## Files changed

The complete PR changes 59 files (+5,233/−396). The final ownership split changes two production files (+50/−27); its existing tests remain unchanged. All 131 targeted relay-host, broker, and Gateway tests passed. Both CI ratchet commands passed on a disposable merge with main, after reproducing the original 700 → 707 rejection. Fresh delta and branch autoreviews are clean through P2. `pnpm check:changed` and `git diff --check` passed.

| File | Extraction LOC delta | Responsibility |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `src/process/spawn-broker/relay-integration.ts` | +42 / −0 | Spawn the selected relay entry through the process transport, register cleanup before readiness, and await broker socket/IPC handoff. |
| `src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay-host.ts` | +8 / −27 | Call the broker-owned seam while retaining service lifecycle authority and channel validation. |
